Specifically, marking 'Structured typography' and 'Item names... listed systematically' as FALSE is critical because the text is gibberish. The Router did not let the aesthetic layout override the functional failure of the text. I agree with all verdicts.

The 'image_text_auditor' confirmed this with extremely low confidence scores (0.50-0.60) and nonsensical extracted strings ('MILIS', 'TBE', 'hetor'). The Router also noted minor boundary bleeding on the red banner (Severity 1), which is consistent with the 'topology_boundary_auditor' finding a high mask confidence but visually imperfect edges. The 'perceptual_quality_auditor' found no noise/blur, which is correct—the image is 'clean' in terms of pixel artifacts, but 'broken' in terms of semantic generation. I agree with the severity ratings; the text failure is catastrophic for this class.
alignment_reasoning: The image achieves a low alignment score because it fails the primary functional definition of a 'menu': to list food items. While the 'fine_grained_classifier' identifies it as a menu (Top-1: menu, logit 7.72) due to strong layout priors (columns, headers, paper texture), the 'image_text_auditor' proves the content is hallucinated gibberish. A menu without legible text is structurally incomplete. Only 4/9 checkpoints passed (mostly aesthetic/material), while all functional/textual checkpoints failed. The score reflects that it looks like a menu but cannot function as one.
artifact_reasoning: The artifact score is very low (near 1.0) due to the Severity 5 'text_gibberish'. For document-based classes, illegible text is a structural collapse equivalent to missing limbs in an animal. The OCR evidence shows random character strings with low confidence, confirming the AI failed to render typography. Minor edge bleeding on the red banner adds to the imperfection. Although the image is free of noise/blur (per perceptual auditor), the semantic artifact (gibberish) dominates the quality assessment.
